reader.requirement: At --std 85 a numeric report (and data) description entry whose PICTURE has 'S' and to which no SIGN clause applies carries an operational sign whose position and representation are implementor-defined (documented determination DOC-A.1-177: fused trailing over-punch, ibm table by default), occupying no character position of its own (GR3's separate-sign rules do not apply).

edition-consulted.switches: at DialectLevel < 2002 a WRITTEN report SIGN clause without SEPARATE (and a group-level one) is refused COBOL0900 (SR3); an entry with no SIGN clause, the GR2 case, is skipped (sign is null -> continue), so the default-sign path is identical

reader.edition-search: grep CobolVersion/DialectLevel/Edition in PicInfo.SignKindFor, ZonedSign.cs, CobolNum.cs: none; SignEncoding is a compile option on EditionContext (EditionContext.cs:113), not an edition switch
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the default sign (GR2); yes for a written report SIGN clause without SEPARATE (refused at 85, admitted from 2002)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness pins the default sign on WORKING-STORAGE items only; the report-group printable item and sum counter with a default sign are not exercised (probed here)

probes.printed: [12L 12C 0N -123 |] / [12L |]  (PIC S999 SOURCE -123, PIC S999 SOURCE +123, PIC S9V9 SOURCE -0.5, PIC S999 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE SOURCE -123, sum counter PIC S999 SUM -123)
probes.expected: implementor's representation per DOC-A.1-177 (trailing over-punch, 3 positions for S999, no separate position); SEPARATE item '+'/'-' leading (GR3c)

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: a SIGN clause without SEPARATE CHARACTER in a report group description entry requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: §1985:XIII.3.17.3 SR3: SEPARATE CHARACTER must be specified in a report group entry; refusal

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.3.17.4 GR2  (3.17.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: The default (no SIGN clause) signed printable item and sum counter print the documented trailing over-punch at --std 85 and occupy no extra column, so GR3 indeed does not apply. SignKindFor takes no edition; only the SR3 screen of written SIGN clauses is edition-gated.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-037: sign_edge-001 printed [00{|99999999999999999R|1K|12L|] for PIC S999 SOURCE 0 (positive zero fused '{'), PIC S9(18) SOURCE -999999999999999999 (18 positions, 'R' fused), PIC S99 VALUE -12 ('1K'), PIC S999 GROUP INDICATE -123 ('12L'); the '|' at column 4 right after a COLUMN 1 PIC S999 proves the 'S' takes no position (GR3 not applied). Class c: a SIGN clause on the 01 report group (sign_grp-001) and on an 02 group (sign_grp2-001) are both refused COBOL0900 at 85, so no group SIGN can 'apply' to an elementary item and the default case is exactly the no-SIGN-written case. All matches DOC-A.1-177 (trailing fused, ibm table). Edition sites: DataBinder.SignClause.cs line 59 (DialectLevel >= 2002 return) is the reader's site; PicInfo.SignKindFor and SignEncoding take no edition. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.17.4 GR2  (3.17.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.17.3 SR1  (3.17.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1'.
